title: Improvement: E2E protection for Rust Method/Field APIs
status: open — exported offline for authorized human review; no engineering/safety acceptance claimed
note: Re-exported by the implementation stage of the design-mode run. The scope-stage report with this filename could not be re-read inside this session (file-tool boundary); the decision set below is reconstructed from the supplied issue/comments, scope.md, e2e-design-draft.md and review-packet.md and remains a proposal only. No native artifact or accepted design is asserted.
reviewers_required: communication maintainers (C++ E2E protection/verification API owner)

decisions.title: E2E application point / architecture
decisions.question: Where does E2E wrap the data: transparently in the Rust<->C++ FFI boundary (binding-owned buffer growth), as a field of the user wire payload type, or at a payload level independent of communication type?
alternatives: B: header as a field of the user wire type
source_evidence: comment 5601398184 (payload level, independent of communication type)
comment 5632794860 (Method buffers are fixed-size and pre-computed; lockstep C++/Rust size change required)
decisions.why_not_decided_by_agent: Source explicitly says the design has not been discussed; implementing any option would be an unaccepted safety/architecture decision.

decisions.title: Wire format / profile family
decisions.question: What wire/profile family is adopted, and how are shared vs communication-mode-specific fields defined? Method needs strictly more fields (Message Type/Result/Source ID) than Event/Field.
alternatives: one shared schema sized for the widest (Method) field set
shared wrap/unwrap with mode-specific field blocks
source_evidence: comment 5632794860 (Xm profile family adds fields vs plain Event/Field)
comment 5601398184 ('independent of communication type' must not be read as identical wire format)
decisions.why_not_decided_by_agent: Requires the C++ side's convention and an accepted design; AUTOSAR-spec-derived formats are licence-restricted in S-CORE.

decisions.title: Increment staging (Event-first vs shared-from-start)
decisions.question: Is the first increment Event-only and Method/Field later, or one schema sized for Method from the start (avoiding a later breaking change)?
source_evidence: comment 5634513270 (maintainer recommends event mechanics first, method afterwards)

decisions.title: Alignment with the C++ E2E protection/verification API
decisions.question: Align Rust wire format, profile, DataID and error-class conventions with the C++ E2E API once it is published.
source_evidence: comment 5634513270 (C++ E2E API is being designed and will be shared; Rust must derive its API from it)
decisions.native_obligation: Unknown until the C++ API exists; blocked external dependency
decisions.blocking_on: C++ E2E protection/verification API not published at this baseline

decisions.title: E2E error classes
decisions.question: Which error classes/variants may the Rust API expose, and how do they map to score_com::Error (result mechanism, no exceptions)?
source_evidence: comment 5634513270 ('error classes will be restricted to what C++ provides')
decisions.why_not_decided_by_agent: Rust taxonomy may not be invented independently of C++.

decisions.title: Prerequisite: Rust Method<T>/Field<T> API (#782)
decisions.question: When does the Rust Method<T>/Field<T> public API land, since E2E cannot attach to APIs the interface! macro currently rejects?

decisions.title: Requirements / architecture impact
decisions.question: Are requirements/architecture affected? Is a new requirement work product needed, or do existing IDs (FEAT_SafeCommunication@1 + FEAT_DataCorruption/DataReordering/DataRepetition/DataLoss@1) provide the trace?
source_evidence: feature_requirements_ipc.trlc (E2E is not its own named requirement)
decisions.native_obligation: Proposed derivation only; no accepted trace at baseline

decisions.title: Safety scope of the first increment and licence-clean mechanism
decisions.question: Is the first pass limited to CRC + DataID checking, or does it include the counter-delta tolerance and consecutive-failure 'apply/reject the call' state machine? Which licence-clean mechanism is used (no AUTOSAR-spec-derived implementation)?
source_evidence: comment 5632794860 (question 4; fork prototype skips the state machine)
comment 5634513270 (AUTOSAR spec cannot be used directly due to licensing; error classes restricted to C++)
decisions.native_obligation: FEAT_SafeCommunication@1 / FEAT_CommunicationASILLevel@1; safety decision reserved to authorized humans
decisions.why_not_decided_by_agent: This is an unaccepted safety decision; the agent must not implement or accept it.

preserved_constraints: Do not implement or accept an E2E design/safety decision.
Do not use AUTOSAR-spec-derived code (licence restriction).
Do not invent Method/Field macro support the baseline rejects.
Preserve native lint profiles, toolchain pins and published statuses.
